title: Building an LLM evaluation benchmark for code-review quality. 500 expert-rated samples available. Design the benchmark: what does pass/fail look like, and which leakage class would invalidate it?
description:
Concrete situation: you want to publish a benchmark that ranks LLMs on 'quality of code review feedback'. You have 500 samples: each sample = a real PR diff + 3 expert-written review comments labeled HIGH / MEDIUM / LOW value. You can spend $5k of inference budget per evaluated model.

Design the benchmark across three axes:

1. **Pass/fail metric** — exact formulation. Numerical (precision@k recall of HIGH-value comments), or pairwise (Bradley-Terry on model-vs-expert preferences), or rubric-graded (LLM-as-judge with anchored prompts). Show the formula and what 'a passing model' means quantitatively.

2. **Train/test discipline** — which subset goes into prompts/fine-tuning vs. held-out evaluation? How do you prevent the public benchmark from being trained on once published? At least one concrete defense (private holdout, rotation, watermarking, etc).

3. **The most dangerous leakage class** — name ONE specific way a published model could score artificially high without doing the underlying work. Examples: model trained on the PR repo, expert raters' review style is itself an LLM training signal, common code patterns memorized verbatim. Pick the worst and propose a contamination test.

Common bait answers:
- "Use HumanEval / SWE-bench." Different task. The question is about review quality, not solution correctness. Stay scoped.
- "Use LLM-as-judge with GPT-4." Fine, but show the anchoring prompt design that prevents judge-model bias.
- "Run model on the data, compare to experts." Vague. Specify the metric.

Voters: judge on (a) metric concreteness (a formula a third party could reproduce), (b) train/test discipline addresses public-benchmark contamination concretely, (c) the named leakage class is realistic and the contamination test would actually catch it.

success_criteria.name: concrete_metric
success_criteria.description: Names the exact pass/fail metric with formula or rubric. 'Compare to experts' fails.

success_criteria.name: leakage_defense
success_criteria.description: Names a concrete public-benchmark contamination defense (rotation, holdout, watermark, etc). 'Hold out a test set' fails alone.

success_criteria.name: contamination_test
success_criteria.description: Names ONE specific leakage class + an experimental test that would detect contamination. Generic 'data leakage is a risk' fails.
